newsitem.title: USA: Firm recalls potato salads due to contamination risk.
newsitem.headline: Firm recalls potato salads due to contamination risk.

text.p: An Illinois company said Tuesday it was recalling certain potato salad products that may be contaminated with an organism that can cause fatal infections in children and the frail or elderly.

Orval Kent Food Co. said the voluntary recall covers potato salad marked with expiration dates prior to Sept. 15 and carrying the identifying code "W7" because it may be contaminated with listeria monocytogenes.
The bacteria can also cause miscarriages and stillbirths. the privately held food maker said.
There have been no reports of illness, Orval Kent said.
The potato salads being recalled were distributed mainly in the eastern and central United States, except Texas, and in Canada and Puerto Rico, Orval Kent said.
The potato salads were also sold nationally in Super Kmart stores, the company said.

At the retail level, one-, two- and three-pound plastic containers of the potato salads were sold under the brand names Orval Kent, Pathmark, Demoulas, Giant, Acme Markets and Marsh Supermarkets, the company said.
The salads were sold wholesale in five- and 10-pound bulk containers under the Orval Kent, Salad Plus, Signature Salads and Signature Delights brands, the company said.
The company's Wheeling, Ill., plant produced the potentially contaminated salads, said Bill Petty, president and chief executive officer of Orval Kent.
"We've found the source of the problem and we've corrected it," he said.
The company was notified of the contamination by a customer and is working closely with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on the issue, Petty said.
